correctness.rationale: Both degree-two characters are distinct for n≥5, are real on rotations and vanish on reflections. The normalized group moment is half a cyclic average. The Laurent support [−12,12] means only frequency zero survives for n≥13. Independent six-step sign counts give the seven half constant terms (10,0,7,0,6,0,10). Cubing |aX+bY|² then gives exactly the stated polynomial in p=|a|², q=|b|² and Re(a conjugate(b)), and replacing the square of the latter by pq−Im(a conjugate(b))² gives the stated phase defect. The aligned polynomial is 10+60x−45x²−15x³, with its unique maximum at x=√21/3−1. Its exact factored gap gives the stated identity and all nonzero equality cases. For 6≤n≤12, n is reached by six positive steps with n−6 twos; for n=5 use (2,1,1,1,1,−1). At the positive aligned maximizing pair all Laurent coefficients are nonnegative, so these aliased coefficients prove strict increase for every smaller asserted order.
residual_risks: The lower-order comparisons are strict lower bounds, not sharp constants or extremizer classifications at those orders.
